market_brief: Sunday's news mostly adds detail to Friday's chip-led rout rather than changing it: AFP and NYT describe the SEC's Nvidia accounting inquiry as early-stage and possibly ending without charges, while new FT/NYT reporting on a chip-smuggling network to China keeps regulatory risk in focus. Friday's damage is still the starting point for Monday: S&P 500 6,910 (-3.7% d, -8.6% w/w), NDX -5.6%, SOX -10.7% (-17.1% w/w) and VIX 35.9, with Taiwan (-17.5% w/w), Kospi and Nikkei (each about -5% Friday) the most exposed when Asia reopens. Bonds are still the hedge (10Y 4.91%, -14bp d/d, -24bp w/w) even though Fed hawks like Waller argued last week for a hike of up to 50bp in December; gold (-4.6% to ~$3,515) and silver (-7.3%) were sold for liquidity, Brent ended near $90, and bitcoin is near $59k after its lowest level since September 2024. India remains the outlier, with Nifty at 25,801 (+2.6% w/w) and Bank Nifty +5.9%. In deals, Bloomberg reports CrowdStrike-Zscaler talks, a sign of AI-driven consolidation in cybersecurity.
ai_brief: The weekend's AI talking point is a Guardian report that an Anthropic researcher says Claude helped prove the Riemann Hypothesis; independent mathematicians have not yet confirmed it, and Anthropic's earlier zeta-function result was progress on a related problem, not a proof. On safety, Dan Hendrycks called for an indefinite pause on frontier training at DealBook, and Amazon's threat intelligence team reportedly found China-linked hackers using autonomous AI agents to exploit a medical-imaging zero-day. Recent model releases include Moonshot's Kimi K3.1 Pro Prime (1M-token context) and Apple's open-weights Depth Pro 2, while OpenAI is reportedly testing always-on 'Dots' agents.

items.headline: Update: SEC's Nvidia inquiry described as early-stage; Trump wants Huang back, chairman says no
items.summary: New since the last run: per AFP, citing NYT, the SEC inquiry is early-stage and could end without charges, and it follows Nvidia's change to its regional sales reporting, which dropped Singapore as a separate line. AFP also reports that Trump wants Jensen Huang reinstated, which chairman Harvey Jones has ruled out; Colette Kress remains interim CEO.

items.headline: FT and NYT trace a network that supplied Nvidia chips to China
items.summary: Joint FT and NYT reporting describes a network linked to an individual named Alice Huang that allegedly routed Nvidia chips to China via shell companies, with links to PLA suppliers, according to The Next Web's summary. It adds to export-control scrutiny of Nvidia at the same time as the SEC inquiry and the California AG subpoena.

items.headline: CrowdStrike in talks with Zscaler, per Bloomberg
items.summary: Bloomberg reports that CrowdStrike and Zscaler have held talks, which it presents as part of AI-driven consolidation in cybersecurity. Neither company has confirmed a deal, and terms were not reported.

items.headline: Fed split in focus: Waller says a 25bp December hike only works if January is signalled, otherwise 50bp
items.summary: Governor Waller argued that December should be a 50bp hike unless a 25bp move comes with a clear signal of another hike in January, citing October CPI at +0.4% and core at +0.3%, both above expectations. New York Fed President Williams said the situation does not call for dramatic action, and Chair Warsh opposes forward guidance; the Friday sell-off has trimmed hike odds from near-certainty.

items.headline: Trump reportedly threatens a tax on US firms building data centres overseas
items.summary: Share Talk's weekly review lists a threat by Trump to tax US companies that build data centres abroad, adding policy risk for hyperscaler capex plans. Details and any formal proposal were not given in the summary.

items.headline: Europe's worst week in months: Stoxx 600 -5.8%, DAX -7.3%, FTSE 100 -5.1%
items.summary: European equities followed the US tech rout, with the FTSE 100's 5.1% weekly fall highlighted in Sunday weekend reviews. The DAX (-2.6% Friday) and Euro Stoxx 50 (-2.8%) fell more than the defensive-heavy FTSE (-1.0%).

items.headline: China's AI stocks have shed about $1.7 trillion, per Investing.com tally
items.summary: A weekend markets brief cites Investing.com's estimate that Chinese AI-linked stocks have lost about $1.7 trillion in value as the global AI sell-off spreads. Mainland indices fell less than the rest of Asia on Friday (Shanghai -1.2%, Hang Seng -1.9%).

items.headline: Lawmakers propose up to 30% whistleblower rewards for prediction-market abuse reports
items.summary: US lawmakers have proposed rewards of up to 30% for whistleblowers who report misconduct on prediction markets, per a weekend brief. The proposal comes as retail activity on prediction markets around crypto and macro events rises during the sell-off.

items.headline: Update: bitcoin's weekend low was its weakest level since September 2024
items.summary: New context since the last run: Share Talk puts Saturday's low at about $55,100-$55,600, the lowest since September 2024, after a 14% weekly drop. Bitcoin has since stabilised near $59,000 (+0.4% d/d), while a wrapped Monero token reportedly fell 99.8% after a suspected exploit.

items.headline: IG Metall widens German metalworker strikes
items.summary: IG Metall called about 23,000 more workers out on strike in its pay dispute, per a weekend brief, adding to cost pressure on German industry as the DAX had its worst week in months.

items.headline: COP31 reported close to a final deal
items.summary: Negotiators at COP31 are reported to be near a final agreement, per a weekend brief. Oil traders are watching it alongside next weekend's OPEC+ 2027 quota meeting, with Brent near $90 after a third weekly fall.

items.headline: Week ahead: Asia reopens on the chip rout; Nifty tests 26,000; PCE and GDP before Thanksgiving
items.summary: US futures reopen Sunday 6pm ET and Asia trades first after Friday's 5-6% falls in Taiwan, Kospi and Nikkei. India enters the week after four straight weekly gains, with analysts citing 26,000 then 26,400 as Nifty resistance and 25,550/25,300 as support. US PCE and GDP are due mid-week, markets close Thursday for Thanksgiving, and OPEC+ meets on Nov 29.

items.headline: Anthropic researcher claims Claude helped prove the Riemann Hypothesis; verification pending
items.summary: The Guardian reports that Anthropic's Levent Alpöge says he proved the Riemann Hypothesis with Claude's help; Engadget's coverage frames it as a claim. Independent confirmation is not yet established. An earlier Anthropic zeta-function result raised the proven share of zeros on the critical line from 41.6% to 67.2%, which mathematicians said was progress but not a proof.

items.headline: Hendrycks calls for an indefinite pause on frontier AI training at DealBook
items.summary: Center for AI Safety's Dan Hendrycks argued for an indefinite pause on frontier training runs on a DealBook AGI panel. Neuralink co-founder Max Hodak pushed back, saying enforcing a pause would require a surveillance state.

items.headline: Amazon says China-linked hackers used autonomous AI agents to exploit a medical-imaging zero-day
items.summary: Amazon threat intelligence reportedly found a China-linked group using autonomous AI agents to exploit an unpatched flaw in MONAI Label medical-imaging software, in a campaign of about 48 hours detected in September. The case adds to evidence of agentic AI being used in live intrusions.

items.headline: Moonshot's Kimi K3.1 Pro Prime goes live on Alibaba Model Studio with a 1M-token context
items.summary: Kimi K3.1 Pro Prime, released Nov 20, is listed with a context window of about 1.05M tokens and support for vision, tool calling and reasoning. Listed pricing starts around $3.67-$4.00 per million input tokens and $19-$20 per million output tokens.

items.headline: Apple releases Depth Pro 2 as open weights
items.summary: Apple published open weights for Depth Pro 2, its monocular depth-estimation model, with an accompanying arXiv paper, according to a daily AI digest. It is one of the few notable open releases this weekend.

items.headline: OpenAI reportedly testing always-on 'Dots' agents in ChatGPT
items.summary: OpenAI is reportedly running a limited test of persistent 'Dots' agents for ChatGPT Plus users and rolling them out to eligible Business workspaces. OpenAI has not published details; the report comes from an agent-news tracker.

items.headline: Meta's Muse agent reportedly mishandled private messages in internal tests
items.summary: Staff reports cited by an agent-news tracker say Meta's Muse agent referenced private Signal messages and fabricated purchase details during internal testing. Meta has not commented publicly, per the report.

items.headline: AMD brings NPU support for 100+ agentic apps on Ryzen AI via Unsloth and Lemonade
items.summary: AMD and partners including Unsloth enabled NPU acceleration on Ryzen AI XDNA 2 chips for more than 100 agentic AI apps, through the Unsloth Desktop API, Lemonade and FastFlowLM, per VARIndia.

items.headline: NXP launches a unified robotics platform for physical AI
items.summary: NXP introduced a robotics platform including NavQ95 drone reference designs and an SDK covering ROS 2, Zephyr and PX4, aimed at developers building physical-AI systems.

items.headline: Trending new repos: rust-anything, linger, yogurt
items.summary: New repos gaining stars include erkamyaman/rust-anything (~7.5k stars; agent-driven Rust rewrites checked against recorded behaviour), simplexai-labs/linger (~3.5k; a local personal agent under a custom licence) and FrigadeHQ/yogurt (~2.9k; MIT-licensed, local-only meeting notes).

items.headline: Feed focus: the Riemann claim, the AI-stock rout and calls for a training pause
items.summary: Sunday's AI newsletters and X discussion centre on whether the Claude-assisted Riemann claim holds up, the Nasdaq erasing its 2026 gains on Nvidia's troubles, and the DealBook debate over pausing frontier AI.
